author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The European Union’s securities regulator warned Thursday that upbeat asset valuations are increasingly disconnected from a weakening economic outlook, raising the risk of an abrupt market correction.

Reuters reported that European Securities and Markets Authority Chair Verena Ross cited geopolitical tension and rising energy prices among the pressures testing investor confidence. ESMA also described operational risk as very high and increasing, in part because advances in artificial intelligence can help attackers find and exploit cyber vulnerabilities.

The regulator repeated concerns that shocks in crypto markets could spread more widely as links with traditional finance grow. Tokenized equities remain a very small share of global markets, but ESMA said wider adoption could alter market structure. It also highlighted manipulation and insider-trading risks in fast-growing prediction markets that allow wagers on elections, wars and sports.

A regulatory warning is not a forecast that a selloff will occur, and it does not set a timeline. It identifies channels through which losses or operational failures could spread if sentiment changes suddenly. For investors, the report adds a cautionary counterweight to high valuations at a time when energy costs, interest rates and geopolitical events are moving together.
dek: ESMA said weakening economic signals, geopolitical stress and elevated asset prices are widening a gap that leaves markets vulnerable to a sharp reversal.
headline: EU watchdog warns optimistic valuations could trigger abrupt market correction
